- *Hybrid** | Detailed | Simple or Waterfall |
- *Startups**:
- Use: Simple templates
- Why: Speed over process, rapid iteration
- Focus: Just enough planning to execute
- *Scale-ups**:
- Use: Detailed templates
- Why: Growing team needs more structure
- Focus: Consistency across teams
- *Enterprise**:
- Use: Enterprise templates
- Why: Governance, compliance, stakeholder management
- Focus: Audit trail, risk management
- *Recommended Combinations**:
- -------------|-----|-----|-------|
- *MVP** | Simple | Simple | Fast iteration |
- *Feature** | Detailed | Agile Sprint | Scrum team |
- *Migration** | Detailed | Waterfall | Sequential phases |
- *Platform** | Enterprise | Waterfall | Large scope |
- *Microservice** | Simple | Simple | Small, focused |
- ✓ Using template > 3 times with same modifications
- ✓ Company-specific requirements need to be built in
- ✓ Specific industry compliance requirements
- ✓ Unique methodology or process
- ✓ Common patterns across your projects
- ✗ One-off projects
- ✗ Learning/experimentation
- ✗ Already-well-served by existing templates

- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- Focus: Just enough planning to execute
- *Scale-ups**:
- Use: Detailed templates
- Why: Growing team needs more structure
- Focus: Consistency across teams
- *Enterprise**:
- Use: Enterprise templates
- Why: Governance, compliance, stakeholder management
- Focus: Audit trail, risk management

- -------------|-----|-----|-------|
- *MVP** | Simple | Simple | Fast iteration |
- *Feature** | Detailed | Agile Sprint | Scrum team |
- *Migration** | Detailed | Waterfall | Sequential phases |
- *Platform** | Enterprise | Waterfall | Large scope |
- *Microservice** | Simple | Simple | Small, focused |

- ✓ Company-specific requirements need to be built in
- ✓ Specific industry compliance requirements
- ✓ Unique methodology or process
- ✓ Common patterns across your projects

### 🟡 [WBS Documentation](../wbs/README.md)

- WBS best practices

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

### 🟡 [Quick Start](../QUICK_START.md)

- Get started quickly

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

- When to use this template
- What makes it special

- Validation steps

- Standard observability (metrics, logs, traces)
- API gateway registration
- Security baseline (OAuth2, rate limiting)
- Database migrations
- CI/CD pipeline
- specific metadata

- ✓ Project/service names
- ✓ Dates
- ✓ Owner/team names
- ✓ Version numbers
- ✓ Sprint numbers
- *Don't use placeholders for**:
- ✗ Company-specific standards
- ✗ Required process steps
- ✗ Compliance requirements
- ✗ Structural elements

- --
- empty string"
- MM-DD"

- *Required Sections**:
- At least one goal
- At least one success metric
- At least one functional requirement
- Defined scope (in-scope and out-of-scope)
- *Validation Command**:
- *100% Rule**:
- id: "1.0"
- id: "1.1"
- id: "1.2"
- *8/80 Rule** (Warning only):
- 80 hours
- *Dependency Validation**:
- *No Circular Dependencies**:
- *Validation Command**:
- *Valid Estimates**:
- *Reasonable Variance**:
- 3x optimistic
- *All Dependencies Exist**:
- *Validation Command**:

- -project-name "Todo App" --template simple
- -from-prd .planning/prd/todo_app.md
- -from-wbs .planning/wbs/todo_app.yaml
- -name "Sprint 42" --template agile_sprint
- Sprint number: 42
- Start date: 2025-01-20
- End date: 2025-02-02
- Team capacity: 300 hours
- User stories with estimates
- -from-wbs .planning/wbs/sprint_42.yaml
- -project-name "Platform Modernization" \
- -template enterprise \
- -github company/platform-modernization
- Enterprise PRD with all sections
- GitHub integration configured
- Validation rules enabled
- assisted WBS generation
- -from-prd .planning/prd/platform_modernization.md \
- -ai
- -name "API Redesign" --template detailed
- -name "API Redesign" --template waterfall
- -from-wbs .planning/wbs/api_redesign.yaml
- all
- --
- ------------|--------------|--------------|
- *Scrum/Agile** | Simple or Detailed | Agile Sprint |
- *Waterfall** | Detailed or Enterprise | Waterfall |
- *Kanban** | Simple | Simple |
- *Hybrid** | Detailed | Simple or Waterfall |
- *Startups**:
- Use: Simple templates
- Why: Speed over process, rapid iteration
- Focus: Just enough planning to execute
- *Scale-ups**:
- Use: Detailed templates
- Why: Growing team needs more structure
- Focus: Consistency across teams
- *Enterprise**:
- Use: Enterprise templates
- Why: Governance, compliance, stakeholder management
- Focus: Audit trail, risk management
- *Recommended Combinations**:
- -------------|-----|-----|-------|
- *MVP** | Simple | Simple | Fast iteration |
- *Feature** | Detailed | Agile Sprint | Scrum team |
- *Migration** | Detailed | Waterfall | Sequential phases |
- *Platform** | Enterprise | Waterfall | Large scope |
- *Microservice** | Simple | Simple | Small, focused |
- ✓ Using template > 3 times with same modifications
- ✓ Company-specific requirements need to be built in
- ✓ Specific industry compliance requirements
- ✓ Unique methodology or process
- ✓ Common patterns across your projects
- ✗ One-off projects
- ✗ Learning/experimentation
- ✗ Already-well-served by existing templates
- --
- *structure** while AI provides **content**:
- Assisted Workflows
- -template detailed
- -template detailed \
- -description "Build OAuth 2.0 authentication system" \
- -ai-fill
- User personas based on OAuth use cases
- Security requirements from OWASP
- Success metrics from industry standards
- -from-prd my_project.md \
- -template waterfall
- Uses 5-phase structure
- Assigns effort percentages per phase guidelines
- Includes phase gate criteria
- Adds appropriate deliverables
- AI-Template Loop
- "Must include security review phase"
- "All estimates in hours, not days"
- "Maximum task depth: 4 levels"
- "Prefer PostgreSQL for database"
- "Use React for frontend"
- "Follow company API standards"
- generated content:
- -from-prd my_project.md --ai
- Effort percentages don't sum to 100%
- Dependencies reference non-existent tasks
- Estimates violate 8/80 rule
- Missing required fields
- ✓ **Structure**: Template enforces required sections
- ✓ **Validation**: Rules catch AI mistakes
- ✓ **Consistency**: Same format across projects
- ✓ **Best Practices**: Built-in guidance
- --
- 01-01"
- 01-15"
- "v2.1: Added security review phase"
- "v2.0: Restructured testing section"
- "v1.0: Initial template"
- --
- -verbose
- name}}
- i 's/{{project_name}}/My Project/g' my_file.md
- cache
- -template-path /path/to/template.yaml

### 🟡 What `init` Creates

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

### 🟡 Template-Specific Variables

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

- ------------|--------------|--------------|
- *Scrum/Agile** | Simple or Detailed | Agile Sprint |
- *Waterfall** | Detailed or Enterprise | Waterfall |
- *Kanban** | Simple | Simple |
- *Hybrid** | Detailed | Simple or Waterfall |
- *Startups**:
- Use: Simple templates
- Why: Speed over process, rapid iteration
- Focus: Just enough planning to execute
- *Scale-ups**:
- Use: Detailed templates
- Why: Growing team needs more structure
- Focus: Consistency across teams
- *Enterprise**:
- Use: Enterprise templates
- Why: Governance, compliance, stakeholder management
- Focus: Audit trail, risk management
- *Recommended Combinations**:
- -------------|-----|-----|-------|
- *MVP** | Simple | Simple | Fast iteration |
- *Feature** | Detailed | Agile Sprint | Scrum team |
- *Migration** | Detailed | Waterfall | Sequential phases |
- *Platform** | Enterprise | Waterfall | Large scope |
- *Microservice** | Simple | Simple | Small, focused |
- ✓ Using template > 3 times with same modifications
- ✓ Company-specific requirements need to be built in
- ✓ Specific industry compliance requirements
- ✓ Unique methodology or process
- ✓ Common patterns across your projects
- ✗ One-off projects
- ✗ Learning/experimentation
- ✗ Already-well-served by existing templates

- Assisted Workflows

- Dependencies reference non-existent tasks
- Estimates violate 8/80 rule
- Missing required fields

- ✓ **Validation**: Rules catch AI mistakes
- ✓ **Consistency**: Same format across projects
- ✓ **Best Practices**: Built-in guidance

### 🟡 When to Use Each Template

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

- specific metadata

- ✓ Sprint numbers

- ✗ Company-specific standards
- ✗ Required process steps
- ✗ Compliance requirements
- ✗ Structural elements

- MM-DD"
- --

- At least one goal

- At least one functional requirement

- *100% Rule**:

### 🟡 PERT Calculations

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

### 🟡 Steps to Create a Custom Template

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml

- Focus: Audit trail, risk management

- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints

- Following Scrum methodology

- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points

- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase

- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

### 🟡 Example 1: Quick Personal Project

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000
- --
- *Create Your Document**
- *Replace Specific Values with Placeholders**
- 01-15"
- *Add Helpful Comments**
- Include API gateway integration
- Standard observability setup
- Company security baseline
- *Document Usage**
- When to use this template
- What makes it special
- Required customizations
- Validation steps
- *Test the Template**
- -template my_custom
- Standard observability (metrics, logs, traces)
- API gateway registration
- Security baseline (OAuth2, rate limiting)
- Database migrations
- CI/CD pipeline
- specific metadata
- id: "1.0"
- *Use placeholders for**:
- ✓ Project/service names
- ✓ Dates
- ✓ Owner/team names
- ✓ Version numbers
- ✓ Sprint numbers
- *Don't use placeholders for**:
- ✗ Company-specific standards
- ✗ Required process steps
- ✗ Compliance requirements
- ✗ Structural elements
- --
- *Required Fields**:
- --
- empty string"
- MM-DD"
- --
- *Required Sections**:
- At least one goal
- At least one success metric
- At least one functional requirement
- Defined scope (in-scope and out-of-scope)
- *Validation Command**:
- *100% Rule**:
- id: "1.0"
- id: "1.1"
- id: "1.2"
- *8/80 Rule** (Warning only):
- 80 hours
- *Dependency Validation**:
- *No Circular Dependencies**:
- *Validation Command**:
- *Valid Estimates**:
- *Reasonable Variance**:
- 3x optimistic
- *All Dependencies Exist**:
- *Validation Command**:
- --
- -project-name "Todo App" --template simple
- -from-prd .planning/prd/todo_app.md
- -from-wbs .planning/wbs/todo_app.yaml
- -name "Sprint 42" --template agile_sprint
- Sprint number: 42
- Start date: 2025-01-20
- End date: 2025-02-02
- Team capacity: 300 hours
- User stories with estimates
- -from-wbs .planning/wbs/sprint_42.yaml
- -project-name "Platform Modernization" \
- -template enterprise \
- -github company/platform-modernization
- Enterprise PRD with all sections
- GitHub integration configured
- Validation rules enabled
- assisted WBS generation
- -from-prd .planning/prd/platform_modernization.md \
- -ai
- -name "API Redesign" --template detailed
- -name "API Redesign" --template waterfall
- -from-wbs .planning/wbs/api_redesign.yaml
- all
- --
- ------------|--------------|--------------|
- *Scrum/Agile** | Simple or Detailed | Agile Sprint |
- *Waterfall** | Detailed or Enterprise | Waterfall |
- *Kanban** | Simple | Simple |
- *Hybrid** | Detailed | Simple or Waterfall |
- *Startups**:
- Use: Simple templates
- Why: Speed over process, rapid iteration
- Focus: Just enough planning to execute
- *Scale-ups**:
- Use: Detailed templates
- Why: Growing team needs more structure
- Focus: Consistency across teams
- *Enterprise**:
- Use: Enterprise templates
- Why: Governance, compliance, stakeholder management
- Focus: Audit trail, risk management
- *Recommended Combinations**:
- -------------|-----|-----|-------|
- *MVP** | Simple | Simple | Fast iteration |
- *Feature** | Detailed | Agile Sprint | Scrum team |
- *Migration** | Detailed | Waterfall | Sequential phases |
- *Platform** | Enterprise | Waterfall | Large scope |
- *Microservice** | Simple | Simple | Small, focused |
- ✓ Using template > 3 times with same modifications
- ✓ Company-specific requirements need to be built in
- ✓ Specific industry compliance requirements
- ✓ Unique methodology or process
- ✓ Common patterns across your projects
- ✗ One-off projects
- ✗ Learning/experimentation
- ✗ Already-well-served by existing templates
- --
- *structure** while AI provides **content**:
- Assisted Workflows
- -template detailed
- -template detailed \
- -description "Build OAuth 2.0 authentication system" \
- -ai-fill
- User personas based on OAuth use cases
- Security requirements from OWASP
- Success metrics from industry standards
- -from-prd my_project.md \
- -template waterfall
- Uses 5-phase structure
- Assigns effort percentages per phase guidelines
- Includes phase gate criteria
- Adds appropriate deliverables
- AI-Template Loop
- "Must include security review phase"
- "All estimates in hours, not days"
- "Maximum task depth: 4 levels"
- "Prefer PostgreSQL for database"
- "Use React for frontend"
- "Follow company API standards"
- generated content:
- -from-prd my_project.md --ai
- Effort percentages don't sum to 100%
- Dependencies reference non-existent tasks
- Estimates violate 8/80 rule
- Missing required fields
- ✓ **Structure**: Template enforces required sections
- ✓ **Validation**: Rules catch AI mistakes
- ✓ **Consistency**: Same format across projects
- ✓ **Best Practices**: Built-in guidance
- --
- 01-01"
- 01-15"
- "v2.1: Added security review phase"
- "v2.0: Restructured testing section"
- "v1.0: Initial template"
- --
- -verbose
- name}}
- i 's/{{project_name}}/My Project/g' my_file.md
- cache
- -template-path /path/to/template.yaml

### 🟡 1. Match Template to Methodology

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

- Includes phase gate criteria
- Adds appropriate deliverables
- AI-Template Loop
- "Must include security review phase"
- "All estimates in hours, not days"
- "Maximum task depth: 4 levels"
- "Prefer PostgreSQL for database"
- "Use React for frontend"
- "Follow company API standards"
- generated content:
- -from-prd my_project.md --ai
- Effort percentages don't sum to 100%
- Dependencies reference non-existent tasks
- Estimates violate 8/80 rule
- Missing required fields
- ✓ **Structure**: Template enforces required sections
- ✓ **Validation**: Rules catch AI mistakes
- ✓ **Consistency**: Same format across projects
- ✓ **Best Practices**: Built-in guidance

### 🟡 4. Template Combinations

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

- specific metadata

- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

- --
- ------------|--------------|--------------|
- *Scrum/Agile** | Simple or Detailed | Agile Sprint |
- *Waterfall** | Detailed or Enterprise | Waterfall |
- *Kanban** | Simple | Simple |
- *Hybrid** | Detailed | Simple or Waterfall |
- *Startups**:
- Use: Simple templates
- Why: Speed over process, rapid iteration
- Focus: Just enough planning to execute
- *Scale-ups**:
- Use: Detailed templates
- Why: Growing team needs more structure
- Focus: Consistency across teams
- *Enterprise**:
- Use: Enterprise templates
- Why: Governance, compliance, stakeholder management
- Focus: Audit trail, risk management
- *Recommended Combinations**:
- -------------|-----|-----|-------|
- *MVP** | Simple | Simple | Fast iteration |
- *Feature** | Detailed | Agile Sprint | Scrum team |
- *Migration** | Detailed | Waterfall | Sequential phases |
- *Platform** | Enterprise | Waterfall | Large scope |
- *Microservice** | Simple | Simple | Small, focused |
- ✓ Using template > 3 times with same modifications
- ✓ Company-specific requirements need to be built in
- ✓ Specific industry compliance requirements
- ✓ Unique methodology or process
- ✓ Common patterns across your projects
- ✗ One-off projects
- ✗ Learning/experimentation
- ✗ Already-well-served by existing templates
- --
- *structure** while AI provides **content**:
- Assisted Workflows
- -template detailed

- -description "Build OAuth 2.0 authentication system" \
- -ai-fill
- User personas based on OAuth use cases
- Security requirements from OWASP
- Success metrics from industry standards
- -from-prd my_project.md \
- -template waterfall
- Uses 5-phase structure
- Assigns effort percentages per phase guidelines
- Includes phase gate criteria
- Adds appropriate deliverables
- AI-Template Loop
- "Must include security review phase"
- "All estimates in hours, not days"
- "Maximum task depth: 4 levels"
- "Prefer PostgreSQL for database"
- "Use React for frontend"
- "Follow company API standards"
- generated content:
- -from-prd my_project.md --ai
- Effort percentages don't sum to 100%
- Dependencies reference non-existent tasks
- Estimates violate 8/80 rule
- Missing required fields
- ✓ **Structure**: Template enforces required sections
- ✓ **Validation**: Rules catch AI mistakes
- ✓ **Consistency**: Same format across projects
- ✓ **Best Practices**: Built-in guidance

### 🟡 Template Versioning

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

- ✓ Project/service names

- ✓ Version numbers
- ✓ Sprint numbers
- *Don't use placeholders for**:
- ✗ Company-specific standards
- ✗ Required process steps
- ✗ Compliance requirements
- ✗ Structural elements

- *Validation Command**:
- *100% Rule**:

- 80 hours

- *Validation Command**:

### 🟡 Validation Fails After Template Use

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

- Standard observability setup
- Company security baseline

- When to use this template
- What makes it special
- Required customizations
- Validation steps
- *Test the Template**
- -template my_custom
- Standard observability (metrics, logs, traces)
- API gateway registration
- Security baseline (OAuth2, rate limiting)
- Database migrations
- CI/CD pipeline
- specific metadata
- id: "1.0"

- ✓ Project/service names
- ✓ Dates
- ✓ Owner/team names
- ✓ Version numbers
- ✓ Sprint numbers
- *Don't use placeholders for**:
- ✗ Company-specific standards
- ✗ Required process steps
- ✗ Compliance requirements
- ✗ Structural elements

- --

- MM-DD"
- --
- *Required Sections**:
- At least one goal
- At least one success metric
- At least one functional requirement
- Defined scope (in-scope and out-of-scope)
- *Validation Command**:
- *100% Rule**:
- id: "1.0"
- id: "1.1"
- id: "1.2"
- *8/80 Rule** (Warning only):
- 80 hours
- *Dependency Validation**:
- *No Circular Dependencies**:
- *Validation Command**:
- *Valid Estimates**:
- *Reasonable Variance**:
- 3x optimistic
- *All Dependencies Exist**:
- *Validation Command**:

- -project-name "Todo App" --template simple
- -from-prd .planning/prd/todo_app.md
- -from-wbs .planning/wbs/todo_app.yaml
- -name "Sprint 42" --template agile_sprint
- Sprint number: 42
- Start date: 2025-01-20
- End date: 2025-02-02
- Team capacity: 300 hours
- User stories with estimates
- -from-wbs .planning/wbs/sprint_42.yaml
- -project-name "Platform Modernization" \
- -template enterprise \
- -github company/platform-modernization
- Enterprise PRD with all sections
- GitHub integration configured
- Validation rules enabled
- assisted WBS generation
- -from-prd .planning/prd/platform_modernization.md \
- -ai
- -name "API Redesign" --template detailed
- -name "API Redesign" --template waterfall
- -from-wbs .planning/wbs/api_redesign.yaml
- all
- --
- ------------|--------------|--------------|
- *Scrum/Agile** | Simple or Detailed | Agile Sprint |
- *Waterfall** | Detailed or Enterprise | Waterfall |
- *Kanban** | Simple | Simple |
- *Hybrid** | Detailed | Simple or Waterfall |
- *Startups**:
- Use: Simple templates
- Why: Speed over process, rapid iteration
- Focus: Just enough planning to execute
- *Scale-ups**:
- Use: Detailed templates
- Why: Growing team needs more structure
- Focus: Consistency across teams
- *Enterprise**:
- Use: Enterprise templates
- Why: Governance, compliance, stakeholder management
- Focus: Audit trail, risk management
- *Recommended Combinations**:
- -------------|-----|-----|-------|
- *MVP** | Simple | Simple | Fast iteration |
- *Feature** | Detailed | Agile Sprint | Scrum team |
- *Migration** | Detailed | Waterfall | Sequential phases |
- *Platform** | Enterprise | Waterfall | Large scope |
- *Microservice** | Simple | Simple | Small, focused |
- ✓ Using template > 3 times with same modifications
- ✓ Company-specific requirements need to be built in
- ✓ Specific industry compliance requirements
- ✓ Unique methodology or process
- ✓ Common patterns across your projects
- ✗ One-off projects
- ✗ Learning/experimentation
- ✗ Already-well-served by existing templates
- --
- *structure** while AI provides **content**:
- Assisted Workflows
- -template detailed
- -template detailed \
- -description "Build OAuth 2.0 authentication system" \
- -ai-fill
- User personas based on OAuth use cases
- Security requirements from OWASP
- Success metrics from industry standards
- -from-prd my_project.md \
- -template waterfall
- Uses 5-phase structure
- Assigns effort percentages per phase guidelines
- Includes phase gate criteria
- Adds appropriate deliverables
- AI-Template Loop
- "Must include security review phase"
- "All estimates in hours, not days"
- "Maximum task depth: 4 levels"
- "Prefer PostgreSQL for database"
- "Use React for frontend"
- "Follow company API standards"
- generated content:
- -from-prd my_project.md --ai
- Effort percentages don't sum to 100%
- Dependencies reference non-existent tasks
- Estimates violate 8/80 rule
- Missing required fields
- ✓ **Structure**: Template enforces required sections
- ✓ **Validation**: Rules catch AI mistakes
- ✓ **Consistency**: Same format across projects
- ✓ **Best Practices**: Built-in guidance
- --
- 01-01"
- 01-15"
- "v2.1: Added security review phase"
- "v2.0: Restructured testing section"
- "v1.0: Initial template"
- --
- -verbose
- name}}
- i 's/{{project_name}}/My Project/g' my_file.md
- cache
- -template-path /path/to/template.yaml

### 🟡 Contributing Templates

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |

- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

### 🟡 PERT Templates

- Schedule and timing analysis (YAML)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- * | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Definition of Done** | ✗ | ✓ | ✗ |
- *Phase Gates** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Deliverables** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Gate Criteria** | ✗ | ✗ | ✓ |
- *Use when**:
- Project has < 20 distinct tasks
- Working solo or small team
- Flexible methodology
- Quick turnaround needed
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints
- *Use when**:
- Following Scrum methodology
- 2-week sprint cadence
- User story tracking needed
- Velocity metrics important
- *Structure**:
- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2
- *Example**: Sprint 42 with 5 user stories and 13 story points
- *Use when**:
- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase
- *Structure**:
- *Example**: Enterprise software implementation with formal approvals
- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management
- -from-wbs project.yaml
- path project.yaml
- -target-date 2025-03-01
- analysis project.yaml
- carlo project.yaml --runs 10000

- What makes it special
- Required customizations
- Validation steps
- *Test the Template**
- -template my_custom
- Standard observability (metrics, logs, traces)
- API gateway registration
- Security baseline (OAuth2, rate limiting)
- Database migrations
- CI/CD pipeline
- specific metadata
- id: "1.0"

- ✓ Dates

- ✓ Sprint numbers

- ✗ Structural elements

- *Example**: Building a REST API with 3 endpoints

- XXX: Story 1
- YYY: Story 2

- Sequential phase-based approach
- Each phase must complete before next
- Formal gate reviews required
- Deliverables at each phase

- --
- *PERT** (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) is a probabilistic scheduling method that:
- Uses **three-point estimation** for each task
- Calculates **expected duration** using weighted average
- Identifies the **critical path** (longest sequence)
- Provides **probability analysis** for deadlines
- Measures **risk** through variance calculations
- Point Estimation
- *Expected Duration (TE)**:
- *Standard Deviation (σ)**:
- O) / 6
- *Variance (σ²)**:
- O) / 6]²
- 10) / 6 = 2.5 hours
- 68% confidence: 13.3 - 18.3 hours (±1σ)
- 95% confidence: 10.8 - 20.8 hours (±2σ)
- 99.7% confidence: 8.3 - 23.3 hours (±3σ)
- *critical path** is the longest sequence of dependent tasks:
- Determines minimum project duration
- Tasks on critical path have **zero slack** (float)
- Delays on critical path delay entire project
- Highest priority for monitoring and management

### 🟡 Optimistic (O)

Best case if everything goes right

### 🟡 Most Likely (M)

Realistic estimate under normal conditions

### 🟡 Pessimistic (P)

Worst case if everything goes wrong

### 🟡 > 90%

Very likely, low risk

### 🟡 70-90%

Likely, moderate risk

### 🟡 50-70%

Uncertain, higher risk

### 🟠 < 50%

Unlikely, high risk

### 🟡 ES

Earliest a task can start (max EF of predecessors)

### 🟡 EF

ES + Expected Duration

### 🟡 LF

Latest a task can finish without delaying project

### 🟡 LS

LF - Expected Duration

### 🟡 Optimistic ≠ Best Developer

### 🟡 Pessimistic ≠ Disaster

- Use realistic worst case

### 🟡 Typical Ratios

- Low uncertainty: P = 1.5 × O

### 🔴 Buffer Critical Path

- Add contingency tasks

### 🟡 Monitor Variance

- Track actual vs. estimates

### 🔴 Parallel Work

- Reduce critical path length

Reflect actual uncertainty in estimates

Break down tasks if variance is too high

### 🟡 Optimistic (O)

Best case if everything goes right

### 🟡 Most Likely (M)

Realistic estimate under normal conditions

### 🟡 Pessimistic (P)

Worst case if everything goes wrong

### 🟡 > 90%

Very likely, low risk

### 🟡 70-90%

Likely, moderate risk

### 🟡 50-70%

Uncertain, higher risk

### 🟠 < 50%

Unlikely, high risk

### 🟡 ES

Earliest a task can start (max EF of predecessors)

### 🟡 EF

ES + Expected Duration

### 🟡 LF

Latest a task can finish without delaying project

### 🟡 LS

LF - Expected Duration

~50-100 MB per directory

< 10ms

< 5ms per process

10-50ms between directories

257 (tested with 257-file project)

(10-20 tasks): < 50ms

(50-100 tasks): 100-200ms

### 🟡 Large WBS

(1000+ tasks): 1-2 seconds

### 🟡 PRD (Product Requirements Document)

Qualitative specification of requirements and goals

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- *PRD-009** | Goal ID is required | Error | ❌ Goal missing `id` field |
- *PRD-010** | Goal title is required | Error | ❌ Goal missing `title` |
- *PRD-011** | Goal success metrics recommended | Warning | ⚠️ Goal has no `success_metrics` |
- *PRD-012** | Metric ID is required | Error | ❌ Metric missing `id` field |
- *PRD-013** | Metric name is required | Error | ❌ Metric missing `name` |
- *PRD-014** | Metric target must be positive | Error | ❌ `target_value: -10` |
- --------|-------------|----------|---------|
- *WBS-001** | WBS title is required | Error | ❌ Missing `wbs.title` |
- *WBS-002** | At least one task is required | Error | ❌ `tasks: {}` (empty) |
- *WBS-003** | Task name is required | Error | ❌ Task missing `name` |
- *WBS-004** | Task needs duration estimate | Warning | ⚠️ No `estimates` or `duration` |
- *WBS-005** | Task dependency must exist | Error | ❌ Task depends on non-existent task |
- *WBS-006** | Priority must be between 1-5 | Error | ❌ `priority: 10` |
- *WBS-007** | Progress must be between 0-100 | Error | ❌ `progress_percentage: 150` |
- *WBS-008** | Parent task must exist | Error | ❌ Task has non-existent `parent_id` |
- *WBS-009** | Child task must exist | Error | ❌ Task references non-existent `child_id` |
- *WBS-010** | Child must reference parent | Error | ❌ Child's `parent_id` doesn't match |
- *WBS-011** | No circular dependencies | Error | ❌ A→B→C→A |
- *WBS-012** | Total tasks should match count | Warning | ⚠️ `total_tasks: 50` but only 47 tasks |
- *WBS-013** | Total hours should match sum | Warning | ⚠️ Sum doesn't match `total_estimated_hours` |
- --------|-------------|----------|---------|
- *PERT-001** | Optimistic must be positive | Error | ❌ `optimistic: -5` |
- *PERT-002** | Most likely must be positive | Error | ❌ `most_likely: 0` |
- *PERT-003** | Pessimistic must be positive | Error | ❌ `pessimistic: -10` |
- *PERT-004** | Optimistic ≤ Most Likely | Error | ❌ `optimistic: 10, most_likely: 8` |
- *PERT-005** | Most Likely ≤ Pessimistic | Error | ❌ `most_likely: 20, pessimistic: 15` |
- --------|-------------|----------|---------|
- *PA-001** | Project duration must be positive | Error | ❌ `project_duration: -5` |
- *PA-002** | 50% confidence must be positive | Error | ❌ `confidence_50: -10` |
- *PA-003** | 95% confidence must be positive | Error | ❌ `confidence_95: -20` |
- *PA-004** | 50% ≤ 95% confidence | Error | ❌ `confidence_50: 100, confidence_95: 80` |
- *PA-005** | Duration ≤ 95% confidence | Warning | ⚠️ `project_duration: 120, confidence_95: 100` |
- Component Consistency
- --------|-------------|----------|---------|
- *CC-001** | PRD requirement task must exist | Error | ❌ Requirement references non-existent WBS task |
- *CC-002** | Critical path task must exist | Error | ❌ PERT critical path references non-existent task |
- *CC-003** | High-risk task must exist | Error | ❌ PERT high-risk list references non-existent task |
- --------|-------------|----------|---------|
- *AC-001** | Max parallel tasks must be positive | Error | ❌ `max_parallel_tasks: 0` |
- *AC-002** | Max parallel tasks ≤ 10 recommended | Warning | ⚠️ `max_parallel_tasks: 15` |
- *AC-003** | Timeout must be positive | Error | ❌ `timeout_hours: -5` |
- *AC-004** | Retry attempts must be non-negative | Error | ❌ `retry_attempts: -1` |
- *AC-005** | Retry attempts ≤ 5 recommended | Warning | ⚠️ `retry_attempts: 10` |

- 003)

- 004)
- *Invalid Dependencies:**
- 005)
- *Circular Dependency:**
- 011)
- *Error Message Format:**
- *Examples:**
- existent task 1.1.5
- AUTH-001 references non-existent WBS task 2.1.5
- AUTH-001", "task_id": "2.1.5"}
- --------|-----------|-----|
- *"Missing required field"** | Field not provided or null | Add the required field with valid value |
- *"Task depends on non-existent task"** | Typo in task ID or task not yet created | Fix task ID or create the dependency first |
- *"Circular dependency detected"** | Tasks form a dependency loop | Re-structure dependencies to break the cycle |
- *"Invalid estimate"** | Optimistic > Most Likely > Pessimistic violated | Adjust estimates to satisfy O ≤ M ≤ P |
- *"Total tasks doesn't match"** | Summary field out of sync | Regenerate plan or manually update summary |
- *"Parent task must exist"** | Parent task not in WBS | Create parent task or update parent_id |
- *"Priority out of range"** | Priority not between 1-5 | Set priority to valid value (1=highest, 5=lowest) |

- *Work Package Size Guidelines:**
- **Level 1 (Project):** 500-5000 hours
- **Level 2 (Phase):** 100-1000 hours
- **Level 3 (Milestone):** 40-200 hours
- **Level 4 (Task):** 8-40 hours
- **Level 5 (Subtask):** 4-8 hours
- *Don't go deeper than Level 5** - Creates overhead, reduces flexibility
- *The 8/80 Rule:**
- **Minimum:** 8 hours (1 workday)
- **Maximum:** 80 hours (2 work weeks)
- *Planning Poker:**
- estimate until consensus

- **L:** 32-64 hours
- **XL:** 64-80 hours

- *"Missing required field"** | Field not provided or null | Add the required field with valid value |
- *"Task depends on non-existent task"** | Typo in task ID or task not yet created | Fix task ID or create the dependency first |
- *"Circular dependency detected"** | Tasks form a dependency loop | Re-structure dependencies to break the cycle |
- *"Invalid estimate"** | Optimistic > Most Likely > Pessimistic violated | Adjust estimates to satisfy O ≤ M ≤ P |
- *"Total tasks doesn't match"** | Summary field out of sync | Regenerate plan or manually update summary |
- *"Parent task must exist"** | Parent task not in WBS | Create parent task or update parent_id |
- *"Priority out of range"** | Priority not between 1-5 | Set priority to valid value (1=highest, 5=lowest) |

- **Level 3 (Milestone):** 40-200 hours
- **Level 4 (Task):** 8-40 hours
- **Level 5 (Subtask):** 4-8 hours
- *Don't go deeper than Level 5** - Creates overhead, reduces flexibility
- *The 8/80 Rule:**
- **Minimum:** 8 hours (1 workday)
- **Maximum:** 80 hours (2 work weeks)
- *Planning Poker:**
- estimate until consensus

- **S:** 8-16 hours
- **M:** 16-32 hours
- **L:** 32-64 hours
- **XL:** 64-80 hours

### 🔴 PERT (Program Evaluation and Review Technique)

Implementation strategy and critical path analysis

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- *PRD-009** | Goal ID is required | Error | ❌ Goal missing `id` field |
- *PRD-010** | Goal title is required | Error | ❌ Goal missing `title` |
- *PRD-011** | Goal success metrics recommended | Warning | ⚠️ Goal has no `success_metrics` |
- *PRD-012** | Metric ID is required | Error | ❌ Metric missing `id` field |
- *PRD-013** | Metric name is required | Error | ❌ Metric missing `name` |
- *PRD-014** | Metric target must be positive | Error | ❌ `target_value: -10` |
- --------|-------------|----------|---------|
- *WBS-001** | WBS title is required | Error | ❌ Missing `wbs.title` |
- *WBS-002** | At least one task is required | Error | ❌ `tasks: {}` (empty) |
- *WBS-003** | Task name is required | Error | ❌ Task missing `name` |
- *WBS-004** | Task needs duration estimate | Warning | ⚠️ No `estimates` or `duration` |
- *WBS-005** | Task dependency must exist | Error | ❌ Task depends on non-existent task |
- *WBS-006** | Priority must be between 1-5 | Error | ❌ `priority: 10` |
- *WBS-007** | Progress must be between 0-100 | Error | ❌ `progress_percentage: 150` |
- *WBS-008** | Parent task must exist | Error | ❌ Task has non-existent `parent_id` |
- *WBS-009** | Child task must exist | Error | ❌ Task references non-existent `child_id` |
- *WBS-010** | Child must reference parent | Error | ❌ Child's `parent_id` doesn't match |
- *WBS-011** | No circular dependencies | Error | ❌ A→B→C→A |
- *WBS-012** | Total tasks should match count | Warning | ⚠️ `total_tasks: 50` but only 47 tasks |
- *WBS-013** | Total hours should match sum | Warning | ⚠️ Sum doesn't match `total_estimated_hours` |
- --------|-------------|----------|---------|
- *PERT-001** | Optimistic must be positive | Error | ❌ `optimistic: -5` |
- *PERT-002** | Most likely must be positive | Error | ❌ `most_likely: 0` |
- *PERT-003** | Pessimistic must be positive | Error | ❌ `pessimistic: -10` |
- *PERT-004** | Optimistic ≤ Most Likely | Error | ❌ `optimistic: 10, most_likely: 8` |
- *PERT-005** | Most Likely ≤ Pessimistic | Error | ❌ `most_likely: 20, pessimistic: 15` |
- --------|-------------|----------|---------|
- *PA-001** | Project duration must be positive | Error | ❌ `project_duration: -5` |
- *PA-002** | 50% confidence must be positive | Error | ❌ `confidence_50: -10` |
- *PA-003** | 95% confidence must be positive | Error | ❌ `confidence_95: -20` |
- *PA-004** | 50% ≤ 95% confidence | Error | ❌ `confidence_50: 100, confidence_95: 80` |
- *PA-005** | Duration ≤ 95% confidence | Warning | ⚠️ `project_duration: 120, confidence_95: 100` |
- Component Consistency
- --------|-------------|----------|---------|
- *CC-001** | PRD requirement task must exist | Error | ❌ Requirement references non-existent WBS task |
- *CC-002** | Critical path task must exist | Error | ❌ PERT critical path references non-existent task |
- *CC-003** | High-risk task must exist | Error | ❌ PERT high-risk list references non-existent task |
- --------|-------------|----------|---------|
- *AC-001** | Max parallel tasks must be positive | Error | ❌ `max_parallel_tasks: 0` |
- *AC-002** | Max parallel tasks ≤ 10 recommended | Warning | ⚠️ `max_parallel_tasks: 15` |
- *AC-003** | Timeout must be positive | Error | ❌ `timeout_hours: -5` |
- *AC-004** | Retry attempts must be non-negative | Error | ❌ `retry_attempts: -1` |
- *AC-005** | Retry attempts ≤ 5 recommended | Warning | ⚠️ `retry_attempts: 10` |

- powered approach to project planning that combines PRD, WBS, and PERT analysis into a single unified document. By following this guide, you can:
- *Generate plans 8-16x faster** than manual creation
- *Maintain consistency** across all planning documents automatically
- *Reduce errors** through comprehensive validation
- *Enable agent execution** with built-in workflow support
- *Integrate seamlessly** with external tools like GitHub, Jira, and Asana

### 🟡 Optimistic (O):

Best case, everything goes perfectly (20th percentile)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- *PRD-009** | Goal ID is required | Error | ❌ Goal missing `id` field |
- *PRD-010** | Goal title is required | Error | ❌ Goal missing `title` |
- *PRD-011** | Goal success metrics recommended | Warning | ⚠️ Goal has no `success_metrics` |
- *PRD-012** | Metric ID is required | Error | ❌ Metric missing `id` field |
- *PRD-013** | Metric name is required | Error | ❌ Metric missing `name` |
- *PRD-014** | Metric target must be positive | Error | ❌ `target_value: -10` |
- --------|-------------|----------|---------|
- *WBS-001** | WBS title is required | Error | ❌ Missing `wbs.title` |
- *WBS-002** | At least one task is required | Error | ❌ `tasks: {}` (empty) |
- *WBS-003** | Task name is required | Error | ❌ Task missing `name` |
- *WBS-004** | Task needs duration estimate | Warning | ⚠️ No `estimates` or `duration` |
- *WBS-005** | Task dependency must exist | Error | ❌ Task depends on non-existent task |
- *WBS-006** | Priority must be between 1-5 | Error | ❌ `priority: 10` |
- *WBS-007** | Progress must be between 0-100 | Error | ❌ `progress_percentage: 150` |
- *WBS-008** | Parent task must exist | Error | ❌ Task has non-existent `parent_id` |
- *WBS-009** | Child task must exist | Error | ❌ Task references non-existent `child_id` |
- *WBS-010** | Child must reference parent | Error | ❌ Child's `parent_id` doesn't match |
- *WBS-011** | No circular dependencies | Error | ❌ A→B→C→A |
- *WBS-012** | Total tasks should match count | Warning | ⚠️ `total_tasks: 50` but only 47 tasks |
- *WBS-013** | Total hours should match sum | Warning | ⚠️ Sum doesn't match `total_estimated_hours` |
- --------|-------------|----------|---------|
- *PERT-001** | Optimistic must be positive | Error | ❌ `optimistic: -5` |
- *PERT-002** | Most likely must be positive | Error | ❌ `most_likely: 0` |
- *PERT-003** | Pessimistic must be positive | Error | ❌ `pessimistic: -10` |
- *PERT-004** | Optimistic ≤ Most Likely | Error | ❌ `optimistic: 10, most_likely: 8` |
- *PERT-005** | Most Likely ≤ Pessimistic | Error | ❌ `most_likely: 20, pessimistic: 15` |
- --------|-------------|----------|---------|
- *PA-001** | Project duration must be positive | Error | ❌ `project_duration: -5` |
- *PA-002** | 50% confidence must be positive | Error | ❌ `confidence_50: -10` |
- *PA-003** | 95% confidence must be positive | Error | ❌ `confidence_95: -20` |
- *PA-004** | 50% ≤ 95% confidence | Error | ❌ `confidence_50: 100, confidence_95: 80` |
- *PA-005** | Duration ≤ 95% confidence | Warning | ⚠️ `project_duration: 120, confidence_95: 100` |
- Component Consistency
- --------|-------------|----------|---------|
- *CC-001** | PRD requirement task must exist | Error | ❌ Requirement references non-existent WBS task |
- *CC-002** | Critical path task must exist | Error | ❌ PERT critical path references non-existent task |
- *CC-003** | High-risk task must exist | Error | ❌ PERT high-risk list references non-existent task |
- --------|-------------|----------|---------|
- *AC-001** | Max parallel tasks must be positive | Error | ❌ `max_parallel_tasks: 0` |
- *AC-002** | Max parallel tasks ≤ 10 recommended | Warning | ⚠️ `max_parallel_tasks: 15` |
- *AC-003** | Timeout must be positive | Error | ❌ `timeout_hours: -5` |
- *AC-004** | Retry attempts must be non-negative | Error | ❌ `retry_attempts: -1` |
- *AC-005** | Retry attempts ≤ 5 recommended | Warning | ⚠️ `retry_attempts: 10` |
- *Missing Required Fields:**
- 003)

- 004)
- *Invalid Dependencies:**
- 005)
- *Circular Dependency:**
- 011)
- *Error Message Format:**
- *Examples:**
- existent task 1.1.5
- AUTH-001 references non-existent WBS task 2.1.5
- AUTH-001", "task_id": "2.1.5"}
- --------|-----------|-----|
- *"Missing required field"** | Field not provided or null | Add the required field with valid value |
- *"Task depends on non-existent task"** | Typo in task ID or task not yet created | Fix task ID or create the dependency first |
- *"Circular dependency detected"** | Tasks form a dependency loop | Re-structure dependencies to break the cycle |
- *"Invalid estimate"** | Optimistic > Most Likely > Pessimistic violated | Adjust estimates to satisfy O ≤ M ≤ P |
- *"Total tasks doesn't match"** | Summary field out of sync | Regenerate plan or manually update summary |
- *"Parent task must exist"** | Parent task not in WBS | Create parent task or update parent_id |
- *"Priority out of range"** | Priority not between 1-5 | Set priority to valid value (1=highest, 5=lowest) |

- --
- powered approach to project planning that combines PRD, WBS, and PERT analysis into a single unified document. By following this guide, you can:
- *Generate plans 8-16x faster** than manual creation
- *Maintain consistency** across all planning documents automatically
- *Reduce errors** through comprehensive validation
- *Enable agent execution** with built-in workflow support
- *Integrate seamlessly** with external tools like GitHub, Jira, and Asana
- *Next Steps:**
- minute quick start tutorial

### 🟡 Most Likely (M):

Realistic expectation (50th percentile)

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- *PRD-009** | Goal ID is required | Error | ❌ Goal missing `id` field |
- *PRD-010** | Goal title is required | Error | ❌ Goal missing `title` |
- *PRD-011** | Goal success metrics recommended | Warning | ⚠️ Goal has no `success_metrics` |
- *PRD-012** | Metric ID is required | Error | ❌ Metric missing `id` field |
- *PRD-013** | Metric name is required | Error | ❌ Metric missing `name` |
- *PRD-014** | Metric target must be positive | Error | ❌ `target_value: -10` |
- --------|-------------|----------|---------|
- *WBS-001** | WBS title is required | Error | ❌ Missing `wbs.title` |
- *WBS-002** | At least one task is required | Error | ❌ `tasks: {}` (empty) |
- *WBS-003** | Task name is required | Error | ❌ Task missing `name` |
- *WBS-004** | Task needs duration estimate | Warning | ⚠️ No `estimates` or `duration` |
- *WBS-005** | Task dependency must exist | Error | ❌ Task depends on non-existent task |
- *WBS-006** | Priority must be between 1-5 | Error | ❌ `priority: 10` |
- *WBS-007** | Progress must be between 0-100 | Error | ❌ `progress_percentage: 150` |
- *WBS-008** | Parent task must exist | Error | ❌ Task has non-existent `parent_id` |
- *WBS-009** | Child task must exist | Error | ❌ Task references non-existent `child_id` |
- *WBS-010** | Child must reference parent | Error | ❌ Child's `parent_id` doesn't match |
- *WBS-011** | No circular dependencies | Error | ❌ A→B→C→A |
- *WBS-012** | Total tasks should match count | Warning | ⚠️ `total_tasks: 50` but only 47 tasks |
- *WBS-013** | Total hours should match sum | Warning | ⚠️ Sum doesn't match `total_estimated_hours` |
- --------|-------------|----------|---------|
- *PERT-001** | Optimistic must be positive | Error | ❌ `optimistic: -5` |
- *PERT-002** | Most likely must be positive | Error | ❌ `most_likely: 0` |
- *PERT-003** | Pessimistic must be positive | Error | ❌ `pessimistic: -10` |
- *PERT-004** | Optimistic ≤ Most Likely | Error | ❌ `optimistic: 10, most_likely: 8` |
- *PERT-005** | Most Likely ≤ Pessimistic | Error | ❌ `most_likely: 20, pessimistic: 15` |
- --------|-------------|----------|---------|
- *PA-001** | Project duration must be positive | Error | ❌ `project_duration: -5` |
- *PA-002** | 50% confidence must be positive | Error | ❌ `confidence_50: -10` |
- *PA-003** | 95% confidence must be positive | Error | ❌ `confidence_95: -20` |
- *PA-004** | 50% ≤ 95% confidence | Error | ❌ `confidence_50: 100, confidence_95: 80` |
- *PA-005** | Duration ≤ 95% confidence | Warning | ⚠️ `project_duration: 120, confidence_95: 100` |
- Component Consistency
- --------|-------------|----------|---------|
- *CC-001** | PRD requirement task must exist | Error | ❌ Requirement references non-existent WBS task |
- *CC-002** | Critical path task must exist | Error | ❌ PERT critical path references non-existent task |
- *CC-003** | High-risk task must exist | Error | ❌ PERT high-risk list references non-existent task |
- --------|-------------|----------|---------|
- *AC-001** | Max parallel tasks must be positive | Error | ❌ `max_parallel_tasks: 0` |
- *AC-002** | Max parallel tasks ≤ 10 recommended | Warning | ⚠️ `max_parallel_tasks: 15` |
- *AC-003** | Timeout must be positive | Error | ❌ `timeout_hours: -5` |
- *AC-004** | Retry attempts must be non-negative | Error | ❌ `retry_attempts: -1` |
- *AC-005** | Retry attempts ≤ 5 recommended | Warning | ⚠️ `retry_attempts: 10` |
- *Missing Required Fields:**
- 003)
- *Invalid Estimates:**
- 004)
- *Invalid Dependencies:**
- 005)
- *Circular Dependency:**
- 011)
- *Error Message Format:**
- *Examples:**
- existent task 1.1.5
- AUTH-001 references non-existent WBS task 2.1.5
- AUTH-001", "task_id": "2.1.5"}
- --------|-----------|-----|
- *"Missing required field"** | Field not provided or null | Add the required field with valid value |
- *"Task depends on non-existent task"** | Typo in task ID or task not yet created | Fix task ID or create the dependency first |
- *"Circular dependency detected"** | Tasks form a dependency loop | Re-structure dependencies to break the cycle |
- *"Invalid estimate"** | Optimistic > Most Likely > Pessimistic violated | Adjust estimates to satisfy O ≤ M ≤ P |
- *"Total tasks doesn't match"** | Summary field out of sync | Regenerate plan or manually update summary |
- *"Parent task must exist"** | Parent task not in WBS | Create parent task or update parent_id |
- *"Priority out of range"** | Priority not between 1-5 | Set priority to valid value (1=highest, 5=lowest) |

- *Start with Why:** Always begin with the problem statement
- *One Page Summary:** Include an executive summary at the top
- *Quantifiable Metrics:** Every goal needs measurable success criteria
- *Prioritize Everything:** Use MoSCoW (Must/Should/Could/Won't) method
- *User Stories:** Include user stories for each major feature

- *Work Package Size Guidelines:**
- **Level 1 (Project):** 500-5000 hours
- **Level 2 (Phase):** 100-1000 hours
- **Level 3 (Milestone):** 40-200 hours
- **Level 4 (Task):** 8-40 hours
- **Level 5 (Subtask):** 4-8 hours
- *Don't go deeper than Level 5** - Creates overhead, reduces flexibility
- *The 8/80 Rule:**
- **Minimum:** 8 hours (1 workday)
- **Maximum:** 80 hours (2 work weeks)
- *Planning Poker:**
- estimate until consensus
- *T-Shirt Sizing:**
- **XS:** 4-8 hours
- **S:** 8-16 hours
- **M:** 16-32 hours
- **L:** 32-64 hours
- **XL:** 64-80 hours
- Shirt Size M (16-32 hours):
- Optimistic: 16 hours

- Pessimistic: 32 hours

- powered approach to project planning that combines PRD, WBS, and PERT analysis into a single unified document. By following this guide, you can:
- *Generate plans 8-16x faster** than manual creation
- *Maintain consistency** across all planning documents automatically
- *Reduce errors** through comprehensive validation
- *Enable agent execution** with built-in workflow support
- *Integrate seamlessly** with external tools like GitHub, Jira, and Asana
